rationale: The exposure worth studying is visible only in social work notes, which take about fifteen minutes each to read, and 120 hours are available. Reading notes for every eligible discharge since 2023 would take several times that, whereas sampling all readmitted cases (or a random sample of them) with two non-readmitted controls per case keeps reading within budget with little loss of precision (c3). Complexity drives both meetings and readmission (c2), so the design measures it from discharge summaries and adjusts for it. The retrieved evidence suggests the attended meeting with a written plan is the exposure to measure (c1).
alternatives: Cohort of all eligible discharges with note reading for everyone (refused: several hundred hours of reading)
Cohort using booked meetings from the activity log only (refused: measures the wrong exposure)
Randomised trial of standard family meetings (deferred: justified only if the local association is meaningful and the hospital is willing to randomise)
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial would answer the policy question directly but needs a signal and a willingness to withhold meetings; the case-control study uses existing notes to test whether the signal exists.

decision.statement: Answer the question with a case-control study: readmitted patients aged 75 and over and two frequency-matched non-readmitted controls per case, with an attended family meeting and written plan read from social work notes and case complexity measured from discharge summaries.
decision.question: Is an attended family discharge meeting with a written plan associated with fewer readmissions within 30 days in patients aged 75 and over?

criteria.text: An attended meeting with a written plan has been associated with lower readmission elsewhere, and complexity can be measured and adjusted for.
Family attendance can be read reliably from notes within the available hours using case-control sampling.
Meetings are booked almost only for the most complex patients, leaving too few comparable unexposed patients.

gates.requirement: Protected senior social worker time for reading notes
gates.evidence: Memo SW-2026-17: 120 hours from November 2026 to February 2027, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Research ethics board approval for secondary use of social work notes with a waiver of consent

alternatives: Cohort using booked meetings from the activity log only
Make meetings standard without a study
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; the ethics gate is unknown, so no note is read until the board decides.

summary: Case-control study recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and waits for the research ethics board.
